**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Bind graph-node hashes to the authoritative event text**

When a `graph.node` uses its event ID as `nodeId` and its text changes during trimming or HTML normalization, this call omits `sourceText`, so `queueNodeEmbedding` hashes `prepared.normalizedText` while the authority record retains the original `ev.text`. The recall adapter now requires those hashes to match, causing the otherwise completed embedding to be excluded and recall to remain `indexing-pending`. Fresh evidence beyond the prior stale-row finding is this producer path's normalized hash mismatch; pass the exact authoritative event text when creating the embedding binding.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep session identity immutable during updates**

When `updates` contains `session`, `kind`, or `_id`, spreading it directly into `$set` lets a request rename the selected session, turn its marker into another event kind, or trigger MongoDB's immutable-field error. In the first two cases the subsequent lookup by the authoritative `sessionId` returns `null` even though the document was mutated, and the session can disappear or move into another session. Strip immutable fields from `updates` and assign `session: sessionId` and `kind: "session"` authoritatively.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reconcile obsolete graph edges when replacing an event**

When an existing event ID is replayed with changed `graph.edge` endpoints or a changed label set, this call only upserts the edges projected from the new payload and never removes edges produced by the previous payload. The authoritative event is replaced, but the old relationship remains queryable and can continue affecting graph traversal indefinitely. Reconcile edges by source event ID before inserting the replacement projections, rather than only adding the new rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Include chunk index in embedding uniqueness**

When `upsertGraphNodeEmbeddings` stores two chunks for the same node, model, and dimensions, their `_id` values differ by `chunk_index`, but this unique index treats them as duplicates and the bulk write fails with a duplicate-key error. Both the helper's input contract and the recall index contract support multiple chunks, so include `chunk_index` in the unique key to make that representation persistable.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject unknown session detail modes**

When a caller supplies an unrecognized mode such as `"visiblity"`, this unchecked cast bypasses both recognized branches and falls into the unrestricted full-history path, fetching up to 100,000 events instead of returning an error or the safer resume view. Validate the value against `full`, `resume`, and `visibility` before selecting the response path.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Apply event retention to derived graph-node events**

When event retention is enabled, the admitted source event receives `expiresAt`, but these derived graph-node rows are written directly and never receive an expiration. For ordinary events the derived row also retains the original text in `extra.preview`, so after the source event expires a duplicate of its content remains indefinitely in the same events collection. Write derived rows through the retention-aware admission path or assign expiration from the resolved connection policy.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count each parent only once per tier during RRF**

When several chunks from the same parent occur in one tier's result list, every chunk adds another reciprocal-rank vote here even though the output collapses them into one parent. Long documents can therefore outrank a better single-chunk match simply by occupying more candidate slots, and those duplicate chunks can leave the response with fewer distinct parents than the requested limit. Deduplicate parents within each tier before contributing an RRF score, while retaining the best chunk as the displayed match.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.
